subject: Post-call: PoC deployment options and next steps
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@cardiogen.com>, Tom Briggs <tom.briggs@cardiogen.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-21T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: PoC deployment options and next steps

Hi Elena and Tom,

Thanks again for the time this morning — good conversation and helpful context on CardioGen's latency targets and compliance constraints. As promised, a short recap and proposed next steps so we can align on the right PoC path.

Quick recap from our call:
- Primary objectives: validate inference latency under realistic traffic, verify data handling for PHI-like telemetry, and quantify per-token cost at expected QPS.
- Deployment tradeoffs to consider: Hosted API (fastest to start), Dedicated (predictable throughput + reserved capacity), Private VPC/on-prem (controls for data residency and audit logs).
- Compliance note: you flagged that SOC2 + strict residency controls may be required if telemetry contains identifiable patient IDs.

Suggested immediate path:
1) You confirm the preferred target for the PoC (Hosted / Dedicated / Private). If unsure, we can run a two-stage PoC: 2 weeks on Dedicated to validate throughput, followed by 2 weeks in Private VPC for residency/compliance validation.
2) Please send the names + roles of the internal stakeholders who must sign off (security, infra, product).
3) Share an anonymized sample of the request payload characteristics (avg tokens per request, 95th pct size, expected concurrent requests) or tell us the QPS target.

I've attached a one-page mode comparison and a PoC slate with proposed success criteria and timeline. Ben & Lauren are looped for commercial and ops constraints.

Next steps I suggest:
- Elena/Tom: confirm preferred path and stakeholder list by EOD Wed (2026-06-23).
- Redwood: we will return a tailored 4-week PoC plan and indicative cost within 24 hours after we get payload/QPS details.

If useful, Ben can run a quick cost-range sketch for Dedicated vs Private once we have QPS.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
attachments: CardioGen_PoC_Slate.xlsx; Deployment_Mode_Comparison.pdf
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@cardiogen.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Tom Briggs <tom.briggs@cardiogen.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-21T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: PoC deployment options and next steps

Rafael—thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Compliance and residency: CardioGen must keep EU-sourced patient telemetry in EU regions and any telemetry that could be linked to patient identifiers must be processed in a VPC with customer-managed keys. That pushes us toward Private VPC ultimately.

2) Stakeholders who need to be involved:
- Security: Elena Morales (me)
- Infra/Cloud: Tom Briggs (cc)
- Product/ML owner: Dr. Priya Shah (priya.shah@cardiogen.com) — she will not be on all calls but wants to see test plan and metrics.

3) Payload: average request ~ 180 tokens, 95th pct ~ 420 tokens. Expected baseline QPS for the PoC: 6 sustained, with bursts to 20.

We like the two-stage idea: start on Dedicated so we can validate latency and costs quickly, then switch to Private VPC to prove residency and KMS workflow. Timeline: we can do a late July kickoff but need a security questionnaire answered before any Private VPC provisioning.

I'll attach the standard security questionnaire (separate email) and will loop Priya once we have the PoC slate.

—Elena
Director, Security & Compliance
CardioGen Inc.
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@cardiogen.com>, Tom Briggs <tom.briggs@cardiogen.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-21T13:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: PoC deployment options and next steps

Thanks Elena — that detail is exactly what we needed. Based on the token/QPS profile and compliance notes, here's a pragmatic PoC slate and who owns what. If this looks good we'll book a kickoff and circulate a short project plan.

PoC proposal (4 weeks total):
Stage A — Dedicated validation (2 weeks)
- Goal: validate tail latency at expected QPS, measure per-token cost at realistic batching and caching, and test model compatibility (KV cache behavior).
- Success criteria (sample): p50 < 100ms, p95 < 350ms at 6 QPS sustained; throughput headroom to absorb bursts to 20 QPS; cost per 1k tokens within agreed band.
- Redwood deliverables: dedicated pool provisioning, baseline load script, perf report, cost sketch.

Stage B — Private VPC validation (2 weeks)
- Goal: validate KMS key integration, data residency in EU region, audit log generation and retrieval, and run the same load to compare latency/cost delta.
- Success criteria: KMS integration completes end-to-end, residency verified, audit logs delivered to your SIEM, and no functional regressions vs Stage A.

Owners and asks:
- CardioGen: confirm Priya as ML owner and a security contact to sign off on KMS/keys + provide the security questionnaire answers.
- Redwood (Rafael): draft runbook and perf script.
- Redwood (Ben): commercial sketch and any temporary credits for PoC.

Timeline (proposed):
- 2026-07-26: kickoff (if security questionnaire reviewed by 2026-07-12)
- 2026-07-27 -> 2026-08-09: Stage A (Dedicated)
- 2026-08-10 -> 2026-08-23: Stage B (Private VPC)

Attachments: CardioGen_PoC_Slate.xlsx (detailed tasks), Deployment_Mode_Comparison.pdf, Cost_Range_Dedicated_v_Private.csv

Ben/Lauren — can you please prepare an indicative commercial range for Dedicated and Private (monthly reserved estimate + PoC transient costs) before EOD Friday 2026-06-25?

Best,
Rafael
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-21T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-call: PoC deployment options and next steps — commercial sketch

Rafael/ Lauren —

Quick internal note: initial cost sketch (ballpark) based on 6 QPS avg / bursts to 20 and the token counts Rafael sent. High-level numbers:
- Dedicated PoC (2 weeks): infra + reserved pool transient: ~$6k–$12k (depending on instance class).
- Private VPC PoC (2 weeks): provisioning + VPC/networking + KMS work: ~$10k–$25k (more ops-heavy).
- If CardioGen wants a steady Dedicated commit post-PoC, a small reserved tier could substantially lower unit costs (we should propose a 3–6 month bridge).

I'll format this into a concise table and attach to the PoC plan. Lauren, can you confirm whether we can offer a small PoC credit to reduce friction?

—Ben
From: Tom Briggs <tom.briggs@cardiogen.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Elena Morales <elena.morales@cardiogen.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-22T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: PoC deployment options and next steps

Rafael — this plan looks workable. We prefer the two-stage approach you outlined. A couple of notes from infra: 

- Kickoff timing: late July works, please pencil in 2026-07-26 for the kickoff call.
- Security questionnaire: Elena will share the initial questionnaire later today. For Private VPC we will require KMS integration and our SOC2 artifacts before provisioning.
- For the Dedicated stage, we expect Redwood to provide a runbook for load generation and a simple script we can run from our environment to reproduce latency metrics.

Confirming: CardioGen proceeds with Stage A on Dedicated, then Stage B Private VPC pending security sign-off. Please send the runbook and the cost table so we can move approvals internally.

Thanks — Tom
VP, Cloud Infrastructure
CardioGen Inc.
